test_title: PYST 54: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 08 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 93 min and 31 min, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the empty cistern gets filled in 24 min. How long will the pipe at the bottom of the tank take to empty the completely filled cistern if no other pipe is then open?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of the cistern = LCM(93, 31, 24) = 744 units.

Individual filling efficiencies: Pipe 1 = 744 ÷ 93 = 8, Pipe 2 = 744 ÷ 31 = 24.

Combined filling efficiency of all three pipes = 744 ÷ 24 = 31.

Efficiency of the emptying pipe = (8 + 24) − 31 = 1 unit/min.

Time taken by the pipe to empty the completely filled cistern = 744 ÷ 1 = 744 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 744 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First pipe (A) fills the cistern in 93 min.

Second pipe (B) fills the cistern in 31 min.

All three pipes A, B, and the emptying pipe (C) together fill the cistern in 24 min.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given time values.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 93
 744
 8
 
 

 B
 31
 24
 
 

 A + B + C
 24
 31
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of the emptying pipe C be E꜀.

⇒ Total Efficiency (A + B + C) = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B − E꜀

⇒ 31 = 8 + 24 − E꜀

⇒ 31 = 32 − E꜀

⇒ E꜀ = 32 − 31 = 1 unit/min

⇒ Time taken by pipe C to empty the complete cistern = Total Work ÷ E꜀

⇒ Time = 744 ÷ 1 = 744 min

**∴ The correct answer is 744 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank and its efficiency is considered positive. An outlet pipe empties the tank, so its efficiency is taken as negative.

Net Part Filled

If an inlet pipe fills a tank in X hours and an outlet pipe empties it in Y hours (where Y > X), the net part filled in 1 hour = (1 ÷ X − 1 ÷ Y).

Time and Work Equivalence

Pipes and cisterns problems follow the exact same logical framework as time and work problems, where the total capacity of the cistern is treated as the total work unit.
